first_impression.reaction: My assistant shortlisted it because guest photos are a leak risk for us, not a keepsake question. The first screen is calm and well written, no prices, no 'dream day'. The word 'private' in the opening line is what kept me reading. Her summary would be: 'Invite-only album, moderate before anything goes on a screen, unplugged ceremony, and a firm line to guests about not sharing.' I read the opening, the takeaways, moderation, privacy, the unplugged ceremony, the destination section and the close. I skipped the disposable camera part and the FAQs.

journey.quote: A wedding photo app gathers those pictures and videos in one private place, so they don't scatter across a hundred phones and group chats.
journey.reaction: This is exactly my concern, put plainly. A hundred phones is a hundred chances for a picture to end up somewhere it shouldn't. For us it would be three or four hundred.

journey.quote: The trade-off is control: anything uploaded may appear in front of everyone, so moderation before display matters most here.
journey.reaction: Good that it says so. In our case there would be no live screen at all, but I am glad the risk is named rather than sold as fun.

journey.section: Moderation and who can see the album
journey.quote: Who can view the album: people with the link, guests you approve, or anyone?
journey.reaction: The right first question. But a link gets forwarded. I would want the next question to be whether it can be forwarded at all, and whether guests can download other people's photos.

journey.quote: Once something is shared online, you can lose control of how others share or use it, which is the strongest argument for a private, invite-only album.
journey.reaction: Yes. This is the sentence my assistant would underline.

journey.quote: The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner treats photos and videos as personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 when a person's identity is clear or could reasonably be worked out.
journey.reaction: Careful and sourced, which I respect, but it is Australian law and we are in Dubai with a celebration that may not be in Australia at all. Useful for the Sydney side of the family, otherwise long for me.

journey.quote: A line on your welcome sign does a lot of work: please ask before sharing anyone else's photo publicly, and we will remove any picture on request.
journey.reaction: Too soft for us. 'Please ask before sharing' assumes some public sharing is fine. Our line would be: nothing is posted, full stop. The page never offers that option.

journey.section: An unplugged ceremony, then uploads at the reception
journey.quote: Many couples ask guests to keep phones away during the ceremony, so the aisle is clear for the photographer and every face is turned towards you.
journey.reaction: Sensible. For us it would extend well beyond the ceremony, but it is the right instinct.

journey.section: On the day, QR cards on tables and at the entrance
journey.quote: Match the cards to your stationery and test every code on several phones.
journey.reaction: This is a job for the stationer or the planner, not me. Small, but it tells me the page is written for a couple doing it themselves.

journey.section: Before the wedding, through invitation, website and RSVP
journey.quote: If the planning load is growing faster than the guest list, our Wedded Concierge service takes it on.
journey.reaction: A little eager, and placed between an RSVP website and a seating chart app. It frames the service as help for overwhelmed couples, not as a team for a wedding of our size.

journey.section: Questions to ask the venue about internet and data
journey.quote: Ask whether guest Wi-Fi reaches every space you are using, from the ceremony site to the garden, whether it copes with many guests uploading at once, and whether the password can go on your cards.
journey.reaction: Practical for a big guest list. What is missing is the other side of the venue: their staff and the suppliers' teams have phones too, and nothing here asks how they are held to our photo rules.

journey.section: Offline uploads and guests in other time zones
journey.quote: A wedding photo sharing app that stays open for weeks suits a guest list spread across continents: friends flying home to London or Singapore can add pictures after they land.
journey.reaction: That is our guest list. Nice to see it is not assumed everyone lives in Sydney.

journey.section: Guest photos at a destination wedding
journey.quote: Venue questions, guest communication and timing sit more easily with one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: One point of contact suits me. Fewer people involved, fewer leaks. But nothing says this person has handled guest photo rules at a wedding where some guests are known.

unanswered_questions: Has the Wedded Concierge team run guest photo policies at weddings of 200 to 400 guests, including guests who are public figures? (deferred business detail)
Would my Wedded Advisor choose and set up the guest album and brief the venue, suppliers and our security team on the photo policy, or is that left to us? (deferred business detail)
Do you work with confidentiality agreements for suppliers and staff? (deferred business detail)
Can a private album link be stopped from being forwarded, and can guests be prevented from downloading other guests' photos?
What happens to the photos stored by the tool provider after the album closes, and who at the provider can see them?
How should we handle venue staff and supplier phones under the same photo rules as guests?

turn_offs_found.quote: If the planning load is growing faster than the guest list, our Wedded Concierge service takes it on.
turn_offs_found.why: Eager tone. It pitches the service as relief for a stretched couple, which makes me feel like a standard client.

turn_offs_found.quote: Match the cards to your stationery and test every code on several phones.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining a task someone else does for me. Minor, but it sets the register as do-it-yourself.

turn_offs_found.quote: It can be, for a playful mood.
turn_offs_found.why: Mild. The disposable camera idea reads as a novelty for a casual wedding; not something I would read past the heading.

would_share_with: My assistant would keep the private-album, moderation and unplugged-ceremony lines for the planning file and send the privacy section to whoever handles our security and the family office. Nobody else.

cta_reaction.quote: Talk to our Wedded Concierge team when you are ready, and for ideas in the meantime, browse our magazine.
cta_reaction.why: The tone is calm and the page takes privacy seriously, which counts for something. But I do not enquire from a blog link, and nothing here shows a wedding at our scale or how the team would hold several hundred guests and staff to a no-posting rule. I would want a private introduction.

top_3_changes: Offer a fully private option on the welcome sign. OLD: "A line on your welcome sign does a lot of work: please ask before sharing anyone else's photo publicly, and we will remove any picture on request." NEW: "A line on your welcome sign does a lot of work: please ask before sharing anyone else's photo publicly, and we will remove any picture on request. For a fully private celebration, the line can simply ask guests not to post anything at all."

Add the forwarding and download question to the moderation check. OLD: "Who can view the album: people with the link, guests you approve, or anyone?" NEW: "Who can view the album: people with the link, guests you approve, or anyone? Can the link be forwarded, and can you stop guests downloading other people's photos?"

Extend the venue questions to staff and suppliers, as a question only. OLD: "Ask how mobile signal holds up across the grounds." NEW: "Ask how mobile signal holds up across the grounds, and how venue staff and suppliers will be briefed on your photo policy."

Suggested edits are exact old/new strings, name no apps, add no fees, commissions, sourcing or vetting claims, and add no new facts (questions and options only)
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: The welcome-sign line assumes some public sharing is acceptable. Layla wants a no-posting option offered alongside it. Is the suggested added sentence acceptable to the editor as guidance rather than fact?

The privacy section is entirely Australian law. Should a one-line note say rules differ by country for overseas weddings, or does that need a sourced fact before it can be added? Weigh against the 0.20 persona weight.

assumptions: Layla's assistant shortlisted the link because guest photos are a privacy concern for the family; Layla read the opening, takeaways, slideshow and moderation checks, privacy section, setup steps, destination section and close, and skipped the disposable camera section and FAQs.
Persona is provisional and not CRM-calibrated, so confidence is 0.75.
The absence of named apps, fees, commissions and supplier sourcing or vetting is a deliberate brand choice and is not penalised in scores.
